h1: How to Register a Private Limited Company in Nepal
directAnswer: To register a Private Limited Company in Nepal, complete the online incorporation process through the Office of Company Registrar (OCR) portal (ocr.gov.np): reserve a unique proposed company name, draft and upload the Memorandum of Association (MOA) and Articles of Association (AOA), verify promoter citizenship details, pay statutory registration fees, and receive the digital Certificate of Incorporation.
author: Lalitpur Advisory Research Desk

sections.contentHtml:
Incorporating under the Nepal Companies Act 2063 follows a structured digital workflow through the OCR portal:

  1. Name Reservation (Name Approval): Create an OCR user account and submit 2-3 proposed company names. Name scrutiny takes 1 to 3 business days.
  2. Drafting Constitutional Documents: Draft the Memorandum of Association (Prabandha Patra) and Articles of Association (Niyamawali) detailing objectives, authorized capital, promoter share allocations, and directorship powers.
  3. Document Upload & Digital Submission: Upload signed citizenship certificates of all promoters, drafted MOA/AOA, and agreement letters if appointing corporate shareholders.
  4. Officer Scrutiny & Correction Resubmission: OCR verification officers review documents for legal compliance under Companies Act provisions.
  5. Statutory Registration Fee Payment: Pay the government registration fee scaled according to authorized share capital.
  6. Issuance of Company Certificate: Download the digitally signed Certificate of Incorporation, approved MOA/AOA, and formal OCR registration letter.

Statutory government incorporation fees are tiered by authorized share capital:

  • Authorized Capital up to NPR 10 Lakhs: Government Fee NPR 1,000
  • Authorized Capital NPR 10L to 50 Lakhs: Government Fee NPR 4,500
  • Authorized Capital NPR 50L to 1 Crore: Government Fee NPR 9,500
  • Authorized Capital NPR 1 Crore to 5 Crore: Government Fee NPR 16,000

faqs.question: Can a single person register a Private Limited Company in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Under Section 9(1) of the Companies Act 2063, a Single Person Company (Ekal Company) can be registered with a single promoter having 100% shareholding.
